purpose: Diagnostic CPU/allocation evidence; profiled App timings are not the final timing comparison.
allocation_measurement: ThreadMXBean thread allocation bytes / 200000 escaping node constructions after 40000 warmup constructions. Four rounds per node class. Every sample retained; construction-only timings do not predict whole App time.
jfr_allocation_measurement: ObjectAllocationSample weights are sampled estimates. CPU sample counts are inclusive or first relevant Clava/store frame, not elapsed-time attribution.
intermediate_findings: Polymorphic read cost reduced; remaining sampled hot typed readGenerated path was default initialization for location, with caller bytecode index 6 on generic get fallback. This motivated direct typed defaults and cached immutable getter hooks.

parser_configuration_probe.description: Eight workers concurrently read declared defaults in 2000 fresh CodeParser configurations with SHOW_CODE explicitly set true; GENERATED_PARSE_ROOT is excluded from eager initialization. SimpleDataStore is unchanged in both cases.
parser_configuration_probe.cause: Default reads insert into a shared unsynchronized HashMap; resizing can lose an existing explicit option.
parser_configuration_probe.final_fix: Initialize declared defaults before launching parser workers, preserving absent GENERATED_PARSE_ROOT.

profile_scope: Java worker CPU samples and weighted allocation samples include test work outside App.build; no claim of exact elapsed-time attribution.

baseline.note: CPU profile includes JS test work outside App; class-load durations can nest and their sum is not exclusive elapsed time.

current.note: CPU profile includes JS test work outside App; class-load durations can nest and their sum is not exclusive elapsed time.

final_js_findings: Additional generated bases and states require class loading; generic dispatch/copy still appears in samples. Only 31 baseline and 40 current CPU samples retained a ParallelCodeParser.parse frame, too few to attribute a roughly 100 ms App difference precisely. Class-load duration sums are inclusive and may nest. No exact causal percentage or JS speedup is claimed.
